ayahs.1: All praise belongs to Allah—to Him belongs everything in the heavens and everything on earth. Praise belongs to Him in the Akhirah as well. He is All-Wise, fully aware of every hidden thing.
ayahs.2: He knows whatever sinks into the earth and whatever rises from it, whatever descends from the sky and whatever ascends toward it. He is the Rahim—special mercy for those who turn to Him—and ever-forgiving.
ayahs.3: Those who reject the truth say, "The Hour will never come to us." Say: "Yes—by my Lord, the Knower of the unseen—it will certainly come to you!" Not even the weight of an atom is hidden from Him in the heavens or the earth, nor anything smaller or greater, but it is recorded in a clear Book.
ayahs.4: So He may reward those who have iman and do good: forgiveness and a generous, honourable provision in the Akhirah.
ayahs.5: As for those who work to discredit Our ayahs—signs and revelations—they will face a torment of crushing pain.
ayahs.6: Those given knowledge clearly see that what was revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, and that it guides to the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy.
ayahs.7: Those who reject the truth mock one another: "Shall we show you a man who claims that after you have been utterly scattered as dust you will be raised as a new creation?"
ayahs.8: "Has he invented a lie against Allah, or is he mad?" In truth, those who do not believe in the Akhirah are heading for torment and have strayed farthest from the right path.
ayahs.9: Have they not looked at the heavens and the earth around them? If We willed, We could make the earth swallow them, or drop fragments of the sky upon them. In this is a sign for every servant who turns back to Allah.
ayahs.10: We gave Dawud a great favour from Us: "O mountains, echo his praise with him! And you too, birds." We softened iron for him,
ayahs.11: saying: "Make full coats of mail, balancing the links evenly. And act righteously, family of Dawud—indeed I see everything you do."
ayahs.12: And to Sulayman We subjected the wind: its morning journey was a month's travel and its evening journey likewise. We made a stream of molten copper flow for him, and some jinn worked under him by his Lord's permission. Whoever among them deviated from Our command, We made them taste the torment of the blazing fire.
ayahs.13: They built for him whatever he wished—sanctuaries, statues, basins like reservoirs, and fixed cooking pots. "Work with shukr—gratitude shown in word and deed—O family of Dawud!" Yet few of My servants are truly grateful.
ayahs.14: When We decreed Sulayman's death, nothing showed the jinn he was dead except termites eating his staff. When he collapsed, the jinn saw that if they had truly known the unseen, they would not have remained in such humiliating labour.
ayahs.15: There was a sign for the people of Saba in their homeland: two gardens, one on the right and one on the left. They were told: "Eat from your Lord's provision and be grateful to Him—a good land and a forgiving Lord."
ayahs.16: But they turned away. So We sent against them a devastating flood and replaced their gardens with two others bearing bitter fruit, barren scrub, and a few thorny trees.
ayahs.17: This is how We repaid them for their ingratitude. We do not punish in this way except those who are deeply ungrateful.
ayahs.18: We had placed between them and the blessed cities many towns within sight of one another, with moderate travel distances between them: "Travel through them safely by day and night."
ayahs.19: But they said, "Our Lord, lengthen the distances between our journeys"—wronging themselves. So We made them cautionary tales and scattered them completely. In this are signs for whoever has sabr—steadfast endurance—and shukr.
ayahs.20: Iblis's assumption about them came true: they followed him, all except a group of true believers.
ayahs.21: He had no real authority over them; We only allowed this to distinguish those who believe in the Akhirah from those who doubt it. Your Lord is watchful over all things.
ayahs.22: Say: "Call upon those you claim as gods besides Allah. They do not own even an atom's weight in the heavens or the earth, nor do they share in governing them, nor is any of them a helper to Him."
ayahs.23: No intercession benefits with Him except for those He permits. When dread is lifted from the hearts of those permitted to intercede, they will ask one another, "What did your Lord just say?" They will answer, "The truth—and He is the Most High, the All-Great."
ayahs.24: Ask them: "Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth?" Say: "Allah! One of our two groups is rightly guided and the other is clearly astray."
ayahs.25: Say: "You are not accountable for our wrongdoing, and we are not accountable for yours."
ayahs.26: Say: "Our Lord will gather us together, then judge between us with truth. He is the All-Knowing Judge."
ayahs.27: Say: "Show me those you have joined with Him as partners. No—in truth He alone is Allah, the Almighty, All-Wise."
ayahs.28: We sent you only as a bearer of good news and a warner to all humanity—but most people do not know.
ayahs.29: They ask, "When will this threat come true, if you are honest?"
ayahs.30: Say: "A Day has already been appointed for you. You cannot delay it by a moment nor advance it."
ayahs.31: Those who reject the truth swear: "We will never believe in this Quran or in what came before it." If only you could see when the wrongdoers are held before their Lord, blaming one another! The followers will say to their arrogant leaders, "Had it not been for you, we would have been believers."
ayahs.32: The leaders will answer, "Did we block you from guidance after it reached you? No—you were already wicked on your own."
ayahs.33: The followers will say, "It was your scheming day and night when you ordered us to reject Allah and set up equals with Him." They will hide their remorse when they see the torment. We will put shackles around the necks of those who rejected the truth. Are they repaid except for what they used to do?
ayahs.34: Whenever We sent a warner to a community, its elite would say, "We reject what you have been sent with."
ayahs.35: They would add, "We have more wealth and children than you, and we will never be punished."
ayahs.36: Say: "My Lord gives abundant or limited provision to whomever He wills—but most people do not understand."
ayahs.37: It is not your wealth or your children that bring you nearer to Us. Only those who believe and do good will have multiplied reward for what they did, secure in elevated dwellings.
ayahs.38: As for those who work to discredit Our ayahs, they will be confined in torment.
ayahs.39: Say: "My Lord gives abundant or limited provision to whichever of His servants He wills. Whatever you spend, He will replace it—He is the best of providers."
ayahs.40: Consider the Day He will gather them all and ask the angels, "Was it you these people used to worship?"
ayahs.41: They will say, "Glory be to You! You are our Protector, not them. They followed the jinn—most of them believed in jinn rather than Allah."
ayahs.42: So today none of you can benefit or protect the other. We will tell the wrongdoers, "Taste the torment of the Fire that you used to deny."
ayahs.43: When Our clear ayahs are recited to them, they say, "This is only a man trying to stop you from what your forefathers worshipped." They also say, "This Quran is nothing but a fabricated lie." And when the truth comes to them, they call it pure magic.
ayahs.44: We never gave them scriptures to study, nor sent them any warner before you.
ayahs.45: Those before them denied as well—and these people have not attained even a tenth of what We gave their predecessors. Yet when they rejected My messengers, how severe was My response!
ayahs.46: Say: "I advise you to one thing: stand up for Allah's sake, alone or in pairs, then reflect. Your companion is not mad—he is only a warner to you before a severe punishment."
ayahs.47: Say: "If I ever asked you for payment, you could keep it. My reward is only from Allah, and He is Witness over all things."
ayahs.48: Say: "My Lord hurls the truth against falsehood. He is the Knower of all that is unseen."
ayahs.49: Say: "The truth has come, and falsehood will vanish and never return."
ayahs.50: Say: "If I am astray, the loss is only mine. If I am guided, it is only because of what my Lord reveals to me. He is All-Hearing, Ever Near."
ayahs.51: If only you could see when they are terrified with no escape, seized from a nearby place.
ayahs.52: They will cry, "We believe now!" But how can they attain faith from so far away?
ayahs.53: They had already rejected it before, guessing blindly from an equally distant place.
ayahs.54: They will be barred from what they desire, as was done to their counterparts before. They were all in deep, unsettling doubt.
